newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Citicorp raised to a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Citicorp raised to a buy.

text.p: -- Gerard Klauer Mattison analyst George Salem said in a research note he raised his rating on Citicorp to buy from hold and set a 12 month price target of $130 per share.
-- Citicorp shares were up 1-5/8 to 110-7/8 in early afternoon New York Stock Exchange trade.
-- Salem also raised the earnings forecast for the banking company, to $8.50 from $8.25 in 1997 and to $9.60 from $9.50 "due to strength in emerging markets earnings."
-- "We had dowgraded the stock last summer based on our concerns about growing credit card loan risk. Those risks have now diminished," the analyst said.

-- "At the heart of this recommendation are two beliefs, 1) the bank stock group is in the midst of a structural price/earnings upgrade relative to the market, and 2) as the flagship, or bellwether, stock in its group, Citicorp would likely continue to lead any bank stock rally -- as it has in 1995 and 1996," he said.

-- Salem also noted that Citicorp "derives roughly half it earnings from emerging countries, whose economic growth is more than twice the pace of developed countries. Roughly 60 percent of its profits come from foreign countries. Almost two-thirds of loans are consumer. With this earnings mix we believe Citicorp's valuations should partly reflect the roughly 22 times price/earnings (mutliple) we have calculated for a basket of 12 global consumer products companies such as Procter & Gamble, Gillette, etc," Salem said.

-- "The 12.9 times current 1997 price/earnings (multiple) on Citicorp reflects little or none of the premium we beleive it deserves. At the $130 target price, the P/E would be 15.3 times -- still well below the 18 times to which we believe its P/E could eventually rise," he said.
-- Salem also noted that Citicorp's earnings should grow at 12 to 14 percent through 2000 and a major share buyback program is underway and should continue all year.
